Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) stock is trading higher Tuesday in premarket trading, extending a sharp rally fueled by excitement around the company’s new Muse AI agent and bullish analyst commentary.

Nasdaq futures slipped 0.02%, while S&P 500 futures fell 0.03%.

Meta stock closed up 11.34% Monday, reaching its highest level since January as investors cheered early traction for Muse. Shares are now up about 28% in September.

A Sept. 21 Benzinga report also highlighted the scale of Monday’s move.

Meta gained more than $200 billion in market value intraday, with its market capitalization rising by about $207.5 billion to roughly $1.902 trillion from $1.695 trillion at the prior close, according to Benzinga Pro.

Wells Fargo added to the bullish tone Monday by raising its Meta price forecast to $796 from $640 while maintaining an Overweight rating. The firm cited growing excitement ahead of Meta Connect, where CEO Mark Zuckerberg is expected to outline the company’s broader product vision.

The event includes a keynote Wednesday, Sept. 23, followed by a developer session Thursday, Sept. 24. Meta’s recently launched Muse AI agent is designed to help users complete tasks and pursue personal goals.

Muse AI Gains Early Traction

Piper Sandler senior research analyst Tom Champion told CNBC on Monday said Muse has had a strong start. He pointed to high usage, positive ratings and its position atop Apple’s App Store.

Champion said the reception could strengthen investor confidence in Zuckerberg’s heavy spending on artificial intelligence.

"The market is coming to terms with the fact that maybe Mark Zuckerberg’s investment plans are fairly rational after all," Champion said.

Champion added that Meta already operates one of the world’s largest digital media platforms, with about 3 billion people using its apps daily. He said AI agents could add another major use case across Meta’s ecosystem.

He also described Meta as an increasingly essential advertising platform because of its massive reach.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Analysts See More Catalysts Ahead

Rosenblatt Securities recently maintained its Buy rating and $886 price forecast. The firm highlighted upcoming Meta products, including camera-free smart glasses code-named Luna that are expected this fall. The glasses are expected to include six microphones designed to support AI interactions.

Citigroup analyst Ronald Josey also recently maintained a Buy rating and an $800 price forecast, calling Meta a "top pick" and flagging next week’s Connect event as a near-term catalyst.

Benzinga Edge Rankings

Meta scores strongly on growth and momentum in the Benzinga Edge rankings.

Momentum stands at 78.64, while growth scores 79.79. Quality comes in at 75.36 and value at 46.83.

The readings point to strong growth and momentum characteristics. However, the lower value score and elevated RSI show the stock has become more extended after its rally.

Top ETF Exposure

The Global X Social Media ETF (NASDAQ:SOCL) has a 9.26% weighting in Meta. The Invesco AI and Next Gen Software ETF (NYSE:IGPT) has an 8.43% weighting, while the Natixis Loomis Sayles Focused Growth ETF (NYSE:LSGR) has an 8.12% weighting.

Large ETF inflows or outflows can therefore add to buying or selling pressure in Meta shares.

Price Action

Meta Platforms shares were up 0.57% at $745.48 in Tuesday’s premarket session, according to Benzinga Pro data.

news.content:
Amazon.com, Inc.’s (NASDAQ:AMZN) decision to block Meta Platforms, Inc.’s (NASDAQ:META) AI shopping assistant Muse has sparked warnings that the standoff could signal a much bigger fight over who controls the future of online commerce.

Amazon Blocks Meta’s Muse AI From Shopping

Users trying to shop on Amazon through Meta’s Muse began seeing a message Sunday saying continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violated Amazon’s Conditions of Use, according to GeekWire.

The move highlights growing tensions as AI agents increasingly move beyond answering questions and begin handling tasks such as product discovery and purchases.

While Amazon operates its own AI infrastructure and models, it may also have practical reasons to restrict third-party agents. If an AI agent makes a purchasing mistake, Amazon could ultimately face the resulting customer-service and seller issues.

Read Also: Generac Stock Soars on $8 Billion Amazon Data Center Deal

‘Bigger Battle’ Ahead for Agentic Commerce

Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora said the dispute could become significantly broader as more AI-powered assistants emerge.

"This will be a bigger battle than anyone anticipates," Arora said on X, predicting AI agents from Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL), Alphabet Inc.’s (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) Google and TikTok could eventually compete alongside frontier AI systems.

Arora said platforms will have to decide whether to open their services to consumer agents, strike commercial agreements or risk losing relevance as consumers increasingly rely on a single AI assistant rather than individual apps.

Investing commentator Joseph Carlson similarly argued that agentic commerce will continue regardless of Amazon’s decision, suggesting Meta could direct shoppers toward retailers such as Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) or merchants using Shopify Inc. (NASDAQ:SHOP).

On Monday, Meta and Shopify announced a partnership to enable AI-powered shopping and checkout through Meta’s Muse personal AI assistant.

AI Agents Could Reshape E-Commerce Advertising

Financial writer Oguz Erkan argued that agentic shopping could also disrupt advertising on Google and Amazon by allowing consumers to delegate product searches and purchasing decisions to AI.

Andreessen Horowitz general partner Angela Strange described the development as part of emerging "agent/data wars," as platforms consider whether to block AI agents, negotiate business deals with them, or pursue another strategy.

Price Action: Meta Platforms closed at $741.24 on Monday, up 11.43%. The shares gained another 0.40% to $744.18 in Tuesday’s premarket trading, according to Benzinga Pro.

According to Benzinga Edge Stock Rankings, Meta’s Growth score is in the 79th percentile, and the stock maintains positive short-, medium-, and long-term price trends.

Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) has blocked Meta Platforms Inc.’s (NASDAQ:META) Muse AI agent from shopping on Amazon.com, escalating a dispute over how third-party agents access online stores. Amazon’s 2026 agent rules require automated systems to identify themselves and stop accessing its services when requested.

Musk Questions Amazon’s Ability To Detect Agents

Elon Musk questioned whether those restrictions will remain enforceable as agents become tied to users’ browsing sessions. "Amazon won’t be able to tell whether the buyer is a human or an AI acting on their behalf if access is via the user’s IP address & cookies," Musk wrote Monday on social media platform X.

Muse, launched on Sept. 8, can browse the web, fill forms and make purchases after receiving user approval. Meta says each Muse runs inside a dedicated Secure VM, while passwords and payment methods remain hidden from the agent in protected credential storage. Meta delayed Muse for months while addressing safety concerns before release.

Read Also: Meta's Muse Hits No. 1, Carrying AMD Into the $1-Trillion Club

Amazon Tightens Rules As Agent Competition Grows

The clash comes as Amazon builds its agentic shopping ecosystem. The company combined Rufus and Alexa+ this year into Alexa for Shopping, which can compare products, track prices, build carts and automate purchases. Amazon said in July that active users were nearly double, while interactions rose more than fivefold year over year.

Amazon has fought similar battles before. It sued Perplexity AI over its Comet shopping agent, alleging the tool accessed customer accounts without authorization while disguising automated browsing as human activity. A federal judge temporarily blocked Perplexity’s agent in March, though the company appealed.

Meta Expands Muse Across Online Commerce

Meta, meanwhile, is pushing Muse deeper into commerce. Its launch materials say the agent can check out through Stripe’s Link, with Shop Pay support planned. Shopify now lists Meta as an AI sales channel, and a partnership will let Muse users shop across Shopify stores and complete purchases through Shop Pay.

Venture Capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya warned that Amazon.com, Inc.’s (NASDAQ:AMZN) decision to block Meta Platforms, Inc.’s (NASDAQ:META) AI shopping assistant Muse could signal a broader battle over how AI agents interact with online platforms.

Chamath Warns of AI Agent Blocking

On Monday, in a post on X, Palihapitiya said the dispute between Amazon and Meta highlights a larger problem with the development of AI agents.

"This wrinkle is indicative of a bigger problem: the behavior of agents are still quite naive and help amplify a bunch of issues wrt the direction of AI – most importantly including those of strategy and long term competitiveness," Palihapitiya said.

He added, "I suspect everyone will start blocking everyone shortly. Plan accordingly."

Amazon Blocks Meta’s Muse AI

His comments came after Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse AI shopping assistant from accessing its platform, with users seeing a message saying the agent violated Amazon’s Conditions of Use.

The move highlighted growing tensions as AI agents increasingly handle product discovery and purchases online.

Amazon’s restriction of third-party AI agents could also help the company avoid potential customer-service and seller issues arising from purchases made by autonomous AI systems.

Read Also: Chamath Palihapitiya Sounds Alarm on AI Coding: ‘We Are Turning an Entire Generation’ Into ‘Slot Machines’

Meta’s Muse AI Shopping

Meta and Shopify Inc. (NASDAQ:SHOP) teamed up to bring AI-powered shopping and checkout to Muse, allowing users to shop across Shopify-powered stores and complete purchases through Shop Pay.

Shopify CEO Tobias Lütke and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said the partnership would make shopping with Muse easier, with Zuckerberg noting that more partnerships were coming.

NYU Stern professor and entrepreneur Scott Galloway said Meta’s years of user data from Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp could give Muse an advantage by providing personal context that rival AI companies would take years to build.

Muse had climbed to No. 1 among free apps on Apple’s U.S. App Store but was later blocked by Amazon from shopping on its platform over privacy, security and transparency concerns.

Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL), Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META), and Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) face higher borrowing costs as bond markets adjust pricing for debt issuances funding artificial intelligence infrastructure.

According to financial analyst Nicholas Mugalli, credit spreads have widened across technology issuers as debt offering sizes scale upward.

Spreads Widen Across Major Issuers

Mugalli noted that “bond markets are officially penalizing scale” as larger corporate offerings command wider yields and credit spreads.

Alphabet saw credit spreads widen by 15 basis points, moving from 56 to 71 basis points as issuance sizes expanded from $1.25 billion to $3.50 billion. Meta and Nvidia exhibited similar pricing trends, where $4 billion bond offerings pushed spreads out by 15 to 19 basis points.

Mugalli stated that credit markets no longer treat big tech debt as “risk free paper.” He added that institutional investors demand concessions to absorb the “supply deluge,” creating an “explicit funding tax” on scale.

Read Also: S&P 500 Nears Record High But Breadth Flashes Rare 1929, 1999 Signal — Analyst Says ‘We’ve Never in Almost 100 Years Seen Breadth This Bad’

Capital Needs Outstrip Cash Flow

The increase in borrowing costs coincides with expanding capital requirements for infrastructure. Data shared by Mugalli indicates that total required funding has reached $5.5 trillion, alongside a $400 billion upward revision in capital expenditure forecasts.

Organic cash flow of $1 trillion and incremental equity of $0.4 trillion cover only about a quarter of the total requirement, Mugalli said, while noting that as a result, issuers rely on $2.1 trillion in high-grade bond markets and $1.4 trillion in alternative capital.

Hyperscaler debt expanded 92% year-over-year alongside an 81% increase in capital expenditures, compared to a 4% debt increase across the remainder of the high-grade corporate bond market.

Cloud Revenue and Operating Margins

Despite added leverage, cloud operating metrics reflect top-line growth. According to another X post by Mugalli, Quarterly cloud and AI revenue growth accelerated to 52% in 2Q26.

According to Mugalli, operating margins across AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Corp.’s (NASDAQ:MSFT) Intelligent Cloud converged within a 36% to 41% corridor in the second quarter of 2026, while cloud operating profit growth reached 65%.

Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) stock fell more than 1% in Tuesday premarket trading after gaining 9.95% in the previous session. Traders took some profits near recent highs while weighing fresh signs that agentic AI could drive greater demand for CPU-heavy inference workloads.

Nasdaq futures were up 0.03%, while S&P 500 futures gained 0.06%.

The stock is also trading near its 52-week high after a sharp rally. That can encourage investors to lock in gains, especially after Monday’s nearly 10% advance.

However, investors are also watching a potentially important new AI demand driver.

AMD crossed $1 trillion in market value for the first time Monday after Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) said its Muse personal AI agent ranked as the most-downloaded free iPhone app in the U.S. for three straight days, according to Sensor Tower.

The traction adds another data point to AMD’s argument that agentic AI could expand demand for server CPUs.

Muse Traction Supports AMD’s Agentic AI Thesis

AMD has argued that agentic AI workloads rely heavily on CPUs. AI agents often coordinate multiple tool calls and carry out multi-step logic between model invocations.

That workload structure could increase the amount of traditional computing needed alongside GPUs and other AI accelerators.

AMD expects the server CPU addressable market to grow about 50% by 2030 to roughly $220 billion.

Muse’s early App Store traction therefore gives investors a real-world signal to watch. If AI agents gain broader adoption, rising inference activity could support stronger CPU demand across data centers.

See More: Top Momentum Stocks

Technical Analysis

AMD remains in a strong uptrend. The stock is trading 22.1% above its 20-day simple moving average of $497.87. It is also 70.4% above its 200-day SMA of $356.63.

Those gaps show strong momentum. However, they also suggest the stock is trading well above its longer-term trend.

AMD’s relative strength index stands at 72.63. An RSI above 70 typically signals overbought conditions and can precede consolidation or a pullback.

Still, the moving-average structure remains bullish. The 20-day SMA is above the 50-day SMA, while the 50-day SMA remains above the 200-day SMA.

The RSI moved into overbought territory in September. Meanwhile, the stock continued its latest leg higher after forming a swing low in July.

Key support: About $498, near the 20-day moving average and an area where buyers could look for support.

Analyst Outlook

AMD trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of about 157 times, reflecting the market’s high growth expectations. The stock carries a Buy consensus rating with an average price forecast of $604.

Recent analyst actions include Piper Sandler initiating coverage with an Overweight rating and a $600 price target on Sept. 10. Raymond James upgraded AMD to Strong Buy and raised its target to $641 on Aug. 25. BMO Capital initiated coverage with an Outperform rating and a $550 target on Aug. 21.

Benzinga Edge Rankings

The Benzinga Edge scorecard highlights AMD’s strong momentum, growth and quality scores.

AMD has a Momentum score of 99.26, a Quality score of 95.33 and a Growth score of 95.61.

However, its Value score is just 3.46. That reflects the premium investors are paying for AMD’s expected growth.

Overall, AMD’s Edge scores point to strong momentum and growth. However, its elevated valuation and overbought RSI could leave the stock more vulnerable to pullbacks.

Top ETF Exposure

The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) has an 8.74% weighting in AMD. The First Trust Nasdaq Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:FTXL) has a 6.79% weighting, while the Pacer Data and Digital Revolution ETF (NYSE:TRFK) has a 6.52% weighting.

AMD’s sizable weight in these funds means large ETF inflows or outflows can contribute to buying or selling pressure in the stock.

Shopify Inc. (NASDAQ:SHOP) stock gained Tuesday following the announcement of a partnership with Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META).

The agreement integrates Shopify’s e-commerce infrastructure with Meta’s Muse personal AI agent, allowing users to shop across Shopify-powered merchants and process purchases via Shop Pay.

Nasdaq futures are up 0.07% while S&P 500 futures have gained 0.07%.

Partnership Integrates Shop Pay Into Meta Muse

The deal enables autonomous, AI-driven purchasing capabilities through Shop Pay, Shopify’s accelerated checkout tool that stores customer payment and delivery information.

Shopify CEO Tobias Lütke announced the partnership on X on Monday, describing it as an effort to create an “easy and delightful way to shop and check out with Muse.” Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg confirmed the integration on X early Tuesday.

“Teaming up with Shopify to make shopping and checkout easier in Muse,” Zuckerberg wrote. “Shoppers find more. Shops sell more. More partnerships like this coming soon.”

Read Also: Stock Market Today: S&P 500 Futures Gain, Nasdaq 100 Slips as Trump Administration Targets Iranian Airlines

From a trend perspective, Shopify is trading above its major moving averages, sitting 1.9% above the 20-day SMA ($139.31), 4.1% above the 50-day SMA ($136.38), and 9% above the 200-day SMA ($130.25). That alignment keeps the intermediate trend constructive, with the 20-day SMA above the 50-day SMA (bullish) and the golden cross (50-day above 200-day) still in place since August.

Momentum is more "reset than stretched," with RSI at 51.09, which signals neutral conditions rather than an overbought chase. In plain terms, RSI helps gauge whether buying or selling has become extended; near-50 readings often show a stock in balance and more sensitive to breakouts from nearby levels.

  • Key Resistance: $156.50 — a nearby pivot area where upside attempts can stall if buyers can’t build follow-through

Zooming out, the stock is still down 12.22% over the past 12 months, which helps explain why rallies can face overhead supply even as the moving-average structure improves. Monday was a great day if your name is Mark Zuckerberg or you own Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) stock. Here’s how much, in dollars, Meta’s strong stock performance helped CEO Zuckerberg’s wealth grow.

Mark Zuckerberg’s Wealth Gains

Meta stock soared 11.4% to close at $741.24 on Monday, a move that was helped by the strength of the company’s recently released Muse AI personal agent.

With the stock movement, Zuckerberg added $27.3 billion to his wealth, increasing his net worth by 11.9% to $255.4 billion, according to Forbes.

Zuckerberg is the sixth-richest person in the world, but on Monday he outpaced all 10 of the top billionaires combined.

The other nine richest people in the world gained a combined $24.14 billion, less than the $27.3 billion Zuckerberg added to his own net worth.

Ranking second on the day was Larry Page, a Google co-founder, who added $5.2 billion to his net worth. Page ranks third with a net worth of $291 billion.

Monday’s gain wasn’t enough for Zuckerberg to join the top five richest, but it got him closer to Sergey Brin, who is worth $267.7 billion and rounds out the top five.

Read Also: Meta's Muse Hits No. 1, Carrying AMD Into the $1-Trillion Club

Meta Stock in the Spotlight

Meta stock could remain in the spotlight over the coming days. The launch of Muse, a personal AI agent to assist users with tasks and goals, has been well received. Muse is the most downloaded free iPhone app in the United States in recent days.

The social media and AI company is also set to host Meta Connect on Sept. 23 and Sept. 24, an event that will feature speeches from Meta executives and partners and could show investors where the company is headed in the future when it comes to AI and other growth areas.

Through a Freedom of Information Act request, Public Citizen on Saturday highlighted separate drug pricing agreements between the U.S. government and major pharmaceutical manufacturers, warning that these pacts could inflate medication costs globally.

The nonprofit consumer advocacy organization revealed separate ‘Most Favored Nation’ contracts signed under President Donald Trump, cautioning that ambiguous provisions may encourage pharmaceutical companies to charge foreign consumers higher prices or discontinue overseas sales to maintain elevated pricing in America.

Read Also: Trump's Drug Pricing Deals Could Lead To $529 Billion Savings For The Economy Over The Decade: Report

Unredacted FOIA Records Reveal Secret Deals

A Freedom of Information Act request over the weekend surfaced confidential pacts involving Pfizer Inc. (NYSE:PFE) and Eli Lilly and Co. (NYSE:LLY).

Public Citizen indicated that heavy redactions continue to hinder public evaluation regarding the true financial consequences of these administration agreements.

The oversight body specifically flagged unanswered questions regarding GLP-1 weight-loss medications manufactured by Lilly and Novo Nordisk A/S (NYSE:NVO).

Public Citizen also questioned the truthfulness and timing of prior public statements concerning Pfizer.

In 2025, Pfizer became the first Big Pharma firm to finalize a Most Favored Nation deal with the executive branch.

In September, an additional nine pharmaceutical companies signed drug pricing agreements with the U.S. government.

Missing Medicaid Negotiation Criteria Under GENEROUS

While Public Citizen supports efforts aimed at reducing domestic medicine costs, the organization noted that corporate commentary regarding bottom-line impacts indicates Trump overstated his drug policy achievements.

Neither Pfizer nor Lilly provided specific details explaining how the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services will establish coverage standards under the GENEROUS initiative for Medicaid.

These missing terms remain vital for state officials deciding program participation and evaluating patient qualification.

Under GENEROUS, state agencies must adopt federally mandated criteria, including step therapy or prior authorization requirements.

CMS could potentially negotiate coverage rules forcing states to treat substantially larger patient populations without securing a corresponding price drop.

Furthermore, Pfizer promised additional specifics in a separate GENEROUS agreement due by March 31, 2026. However, federal officials have failed to provide that document as of September 17, 2026.

LLY/PFE Price Action: Eli Lilly shares were down 1.32% at $1149.47, and Pfizer shares were down 0.05% at $27.72 during premarket trading on Tuesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

Read Also: Elizabeth Warren Slams Trump as $6.9 Billion in Russia-Linked Payments Reportedly Slipped Through Global Banks Despite Sanctions

On the latest episode of “The Deep End” podcast, co-host Brad Freeman, co-host Shay Boloor, and Future Investing creator Tannor Manson outlined a bullish case for SoFi Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ:SOFI).

Market Mispricing and the Nvidia Comparison

Addressing the stock’s recent market underperformance, Freeman stated that purchasing SoFi stock at current valuation levels “is like buying Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) or Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) at the depths of their” cyclical bottoms.

Valuation Disconnect and Growth Outlook

Boloor stated that SoFi is currently valued like a tech company while trading like a lender, leaving the stock vulnerable to daily swings in interest rates, credit concerns, and lending sentiment.

Manson stated that SoFi management functions as a “compulsive sandbagger” regarding financial guidance, despite management projecting 30% revenue growth and 40% earnings per share growth over the next three years.

Freeman added that market sentiment around SoFi has turned overly negative, arguing that most bad news is already priced into the stock.

Read Also: Bitcoin Hit $85,000 Today — SoFi Stock Barely Moved

Credit Metrics and Cost Advantages

Manson noted that SoFi has expanded to 16 million members and over $45 billion in deposits, with revenue growing at approximately 30%. Freeman cited 90-day delinquency rates of 0.40% and an annualized charge-off ratio of 3.7% as evidence of credit book resilience.

Freeman also stated that SoFi operates with a structural cost advantage over legacy financial institutions because it avoids branch real estate expenses and utilizes its bank charter to fund loans via lower-cost deposits rather than expensive warehouse debt.

Balance Sheet Structure and Capital Strategy

Addressing historical capital raises, Freeman stated that balance sheet optimizations allowed SoFi to eliminate high-interest debt and substitute it with low-cost deposit funding.

Manson explained that SoFi’s loan platform business generates fee-based revenue by originating loans for third-party institutional capital without consuming SoFi’s balance sheet capacity.

All three analysts confirmed they hold long positions in SoFi stock, with Boloor noting he remains invested despite being down 20% on his position.

How Has SOFI Performed in 2026?

Price Action: At the last check, the SOFI stock rose about 5.95% to $17.98 premarket on Tuesday. It was down about 43% over the last year, and 35.18% year-to-date.

Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA) may be a Wall Street stock, but the way investors trade it, is starting to look increasingly like crypto.

Tokenized equities and equity perpetuals are putting traditional names onto digital trading rails. This is creating a market that never has to wait for the opening bell.

The Trading Rail Changes

CoinMarketCap’s Alice Liu told Benzinga in an exclusive email interview that the convergence between traditional equities and crypto is happening at the "distribution layer, not the asset layer." The company’s trending board recently featured tokenized Nvidia alongside tokenized Nasdaq-100, Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL), Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU), Microsoft Corp (NASDAQ:MSFT) and Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG) products.

The category has expanded rapidly. CoinMarketCap tracks 1,851 tokenized-stock instruments with roughly $2.3 billion in combined market capitalization, and about $2 billion in daily trading volume.

Tokenized stocks were turning over roughly 89% of their market cap daily. That’s far above the turnover seen in Bitcoin, memes or AI tokens.

Equity perpetuals are expanding, too. Their share of Hyperliquid’s perpetual volume rose from about 2% at the start of the year to roughly half.

For investors, the bigger shift is not simply that Nvidia can be tokenized. It is that stocks are gaining crypto-style rails — 24/7 access, fractional trading and leverage — potentially reshaping how equities are traded.

Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) has emerged as the leading foundation for sovereign artificial intelligence models built on foreign open-source technology, according to new research from Counterpoint Research.

Meta’s Llama Leads Sovereign AI Models

Counterpoint found that 56% of the sovereign large language models it tracks are adapted models, meaning they are fine-tuned versions of existing open-source models. The remaining 44% are foundational models trained on native data.

Meta’s Llama accounts for 38% of adapted sovereign LLMs, making it the most widely used foreign base-model family. Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. (NYSE:BABA)-backed Qwen follows with a 20% share, while France’s Mistral holds 19%.

Counterpoint evaluated more than 170 models across more than 55 countries as part of its H1 2026 Sovereign AI LLM Index. The firm said Llama was the dominant base model across every region covered by the research.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Analyst Sees Push Toward Greater AI Autonomy

Counterpoint Research Director Marc Einstein said sovereign AI ultimately centers on control and strategic autonomy, but that independence exists on a spectrum.

“A slight majority of ‘sovereign’ LLMs are fine-tuned on open-source foreign bases, so true autonomy is still the exception,” Einstein said. He added that countries are increasingly moving toward foundational models built from scratch using domestic data.

Counterpoint said Qwen is gaining adoption across Central and Eastern Europe, Asia-Pacific and Africa, helped by its multilingual capabilities. Mistral, meanwhile, has gained traction in Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East through partnerships including Abu Dhabi-based G42.

The research also points to growing use of other foundations, including Alphabet Inc.’s (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG) Gemma, NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) Nemotron and DeepSeek, as countries diversify their AI technology stacks and reduce dependence on a single provider.

news.author: Surbhi Jain
news.content:
The next battle in e-commerce may not be over who owns the biggest online store. It could be over who controls the AI agent deciding what consumers buy, where they buy it and how the transaction gets completed.

JPMorgan’s Doug Anmuth sees that shift creating a potentially new revenue stream for Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) — but also a new battleground with Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN) and other platforms.

The Agent Becomes the Middleman

Meta’s Muse is being built to do more than answer questions. JPMorgan says early use cases already span shopping, restaurant reservations, travel planning and other multi-step tasks, while Meta has added Shop Pay for agentic checkout and opened Muse connectors to developers.

That matters because the economics of the internet could change if consumers increasingly ask an agent to complete a task rather than visit individual websites themselves.

Anmuth expects transactions to eventually move toward agent-to-agent interactions, with businesses deploying their own agents on Muse. Meta could then potentially monetize those transactions through commissions or a take rate — essentially collecting a fee when its AI helps make the transaction happen.

The Information adds an important wrinkle: Amazon has blocked Muse from accessing its shopping site, while Palo Alto Networks, Inc. (NASDAQ:PANW) CEO Nikesh Arora has described the episode as part of a potentially much larger battle involving the major technology and AI companies.

Read Also: JD.com Defies AI Disconnect With 'Measurable Progress'

Who Owns the Transaction?

That conflict points to the bigger issue for investors. If an AI agent becomes the layer between a consumer and a retailer, the retailer may still own the inventory, fulfillment and customer relationship — but the agent could influence the decision that leads to the purchase.

The Information reported that Zuckerberg has discussed Muse making money by taking a small cut of transactions. It also noted that major platforms have an incentive to protect their data and customer relationships as agents begin operating across websites and apps.

That creates a new economic negotiation. Retailers may want the sales an agent generates, but they may not want to surrender part of the economics or control over how customers reach them.

The Next Meta Revenue Engine?

For Meta, that is why Muse could eventually become more important than another consumer AI app.

JPMorgan says the company has laid out a path to monetize its AI investments through consumer and business agents, as well as model API access. Anmuth also sees a potential market opportunity in the tens of trillions of dollars beyond Meta’s core advertising business.

For investors, the next signals to watch are not simply Muse downloads. They are business adoption, new connectors, agent-driven transactions and evidence that Meta can establish an economic model around those interactions.

The Amazon dispute may ultimately matter less as a one-off access fight than as an early test of whether Meta can turn Muse into the invisible layer through which commerce increasingly flows.

news.summary: Meta and Amazon are entering a bigger battle over AI agents, e-commerce and who controls the transaction layer between consumers & retailers.

Alibaba Group Holding Limited (NYSE:BABA) stock rose Tuesday as investors weighed the company’s new AI chip and aggressive cloud infrastructure expansion plans.

At Alibaba Cloud’s Apsara Conference, the company introduced the Zhenwu V900, which it describes as China’s most powerful AI chip.

The company said the V900 delivers three times the computing power of its current M890 chip and can scale to clusters of as many as 500,000 chips. The company expects production to begin in the first quarter of 2027.

No international benchmark is available for the V900. CNBC noted that technology analysts in China have compared Alibaba’s existing M890 with NVIDIA Corp.’s (NASDAQ:NVDA) H200.

Alibaba Targets 20 Gigawatts Of Data Center Capacity

Alibaba plans to expand its global data center capacity to more than 20 gigawatts by 2032 as it responds to rising AI demand.

The company has committed $53 billion over three years to its broader AI expansion.

Alibaba also previewed new AI models that it says will be more powerful and use between 5 trillion and 10 trillion parameters.

Tencent Steps Up China’s AI Competition

Tencent Holding Ltd. (OTC:TCEHY) is also increasing its AI efforts, introducing a new image model that it plans to integrate across its products.

Yoon said Tencent hopes the technology will allow AI to perform a wider range of tasks within its WeChat platform, drawing comparisons with Meta Platforms Inc.’s (NASDAQ:META) Muse AI.

Chinese technology companies remain largely focused on their domestic market, but Yoon said Alibaba is increasingly emphasizing global ambitions across AI infrastructure and cloud services.

Chinese leaders are also balancing rapid AI development with concerns about safety, political control and potential job disruption as companies including Alibaba and Tencent push to remain competitive.

Alibaba Carries Significant ETF Exposure

Alibaba represents 1.97% of the iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ETF (NYSE:EEM), 2.52% of the Schwab Emerging Markets Equity ETF (NYSE:SCHE) and 2.06% of the Baron Emerging Markets Select ETF (NYSE:BCEM).

Significant inflows or outflows from these funds can translate into buying or selling of Alibaba shares.

Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) bull and billionaire Tim Draper urged major companies including Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) and Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) to hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets.

He argued that persistent government spending exposes corporate cash to inflation and higher interest rates.

Why Should Companies Hold BTC

Speaking on Bitcoin Magazine podcast on Sep.21, Draper said businesses should keep at least four weeks’ worth of Bitcoin in their corporate treasuries as protection against financial-system risks.

He singled out Apple and Meta as companies that should consider Bitcoin exposure, while pointing to SpaceX as an example of a forward-looking company holding the cryptocurrency.

Draper argued continued government spending creates two potential risks:

  • persistent inflation if interest rates remain low, or
  • stress in the banking system if policymakers raise rates aggressively.

He sees Bitcoin as a hedge against both scenarios and said individuals should consider keeping six months’ worth of Bitcoin available.

In a move signaling deeper interest in crypto, Apple and Alphabet, Google’s parent company expressed interest to hire cryptocurrency developers and other digital asset specialists.

Could Bitcoin Hit $250,000 After The Halving?

Draper reiterated his long-standing $250,000 Bitcoin target, with the next halving central to his thesis.

He compared Bitcoin’s declining issuance to a sharp reduction in commodity production, arguing lower new supply could support higher prices.

Draper also expects Bitcoin’s role to eventually expand beyond a store of value.

He predicted another two halving cycles may be needed before Bitcoin becomes widely used for everyday transactions, estimating broader retail adoption could arrive in roughly five years.

The venture capitalist envisions businesses eventually raising capital, paying employees and suppliers and conducting investments entirely in Bitcoin.

Such an economy could reduce reliance on traditional accounting, auditing and financial intermediaries because transactions would be recorded directly on the blockchain, he said.

Draper sees Bitcoin and AI driving a broader shift toward decentralized systems, challenging traditional finance and other established industries.

His venture firm, Draper Associates, has made roughly 50 BTC-related investments and continues backing Bitcoin companies alongside AI, space, biotech, transportation and education companies.

Conglomerate Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRK)(NYSE:BRK) has gone through several major changes over the past nine months, with longtime CEO Warren Buffett stepping down as CEO at the start of the year and recently announcing he was leaving the chairman role. The news sent Berkshire Hathaway shares lower, but one former hedge funder believes this is an overreaction.

• Berkshire Hathaway shares are consolidating. What’s next for BRK-A stock?

Berkshire Hathaway Shares Undervalued

Under Buffett’s leadership, Berkshire Hathaway stock often outperformed the S&P 500, which is tracked by the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY).

Buffett’s retirement CEO and chairman shouldn’t have a huge impact on the company’s financials, former hedge fund manager Whitney Tilson said in a recent newsletter.

"This has no impact on the company. Greg Abel has been running Berkshire since he took over as CEO at the beginning of this year, and Buffett remains on the board," Tilson said.

Tilson said Buffett made plans for his son Howard to succeed him as chairman years ago.

"Today’s news also has no impact on the company’s intrinsic value."

Tilson recalls highlighting Berkshire Hathaway stock as being undervalued back in August, while Buffett was still chairman.

"My conclusion from back then hasn’t changed. I’m especially bullish because in addition to today’s discounted stock price, I’m optimistic that new CEO Greg Abel can create value via operational improvements and capital allocation."

Tilson estimates that Berkshire Hathaway is "highly likely to beat the S&P 500 over the next five years." The former hedge funder predicts Berkshire Hathaway beating the S&P 500 by two to three percentage points.

Berkshire Hathaway Stock vs. S&P 500

Berkshire Hathaway trailed the S&P 500 in 2025, the last year with Buffett as CEO. Before, Berkshire Hathaway stock had beaten the S&P 500 in three of the previous four years.

Over the final 25 years of Buffett as CEO, Berkshire Hathaway beat the S&P 500 13 years and trailed in 12.

Berkshire Hathaway stock is up 1% year-to-date as of Monday, trailing the 13.2% gain of the SPY over the same time period. Berkshire stock is down around 2.5% over the past five days, falling on news of Buffett leaving the chairman role.

Over the last five years, Berkshire Hathaway stock has posted a gain of 80.7%, outperforming the 74.3% gain of the SPY.

Tilson sees the long-term gains like this continuing, which could mean that the recent drop in price on the Buffett news is a buying opportunity for patient investors.
